project_type: .NET 8 WPF desktop app (WorshipBacktrackPlayer) — multi-project solution: Core (models/services), Audio, Presenter (presenter module: views + presenter-specific services), UI (WPF host / startup project).
build_system: dotnet / MSBuild via WorshipBacktrackPlayer.sln. Note: WPF temp build projects (*_wpftmp.csproj) appear in warning output — this is normal, not an error.
verification_instructions: After each feature: run the build command and confirm 0 errors (4 pre-existing warnings are acceptable: MediaLibraryPanel._currentView, ChordChartWindow CS8604, WaveformEditorWindow._inReviewMode). Then run the test command and confirm 20 TemplateServiceTests pass. These are the real gates; do not substitute grep for verification. Full UI smoke (Tools -> Templates) is manual and cannot run headless, so rely on build+tests plus careful reading.
environment_constraints: Windows + PowerShell. PowerShell does NOT accept '&&' as a statement separator — chain with ';' or run commands separately. All work happens in the worktree, branch feature/template-system. git operations must use: git -C "c:\Users\Quang\Documents\OneWorshipcenter\owc-multitrack-feature-lyric-presenter\owc-multitrack-feature-lyric-presenter\.worktrees\template-system" ... . Relative paths resolve against the parent workspace, NOT the worktree — always use the absolute worktree path. Commit locally on the branch; never push.
contribution_requirements: No AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md/.kiro steering files exist in the worktree. Match existing code style and the established composition pattern (services built in PresenterIntegration ctor, handed to OperatorWindow via SetServices). Keep changes scoped to template wiring + the one Tools entry point; do not modify unrelated features. Preserve the clean build.
key_patterns: Service composition: WorshipPlayer.UI\Services\PresenterIntegration.cs constructs every presenter service in its constructor (e.g. MediaLibraryService = new MediaLibraryService(Path.Combine(appFolder, "Media"))) and injects them into the operator window via _operatorWindow.SetServices(...) inside OpenPresenterWindow(). appFolder = AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory. Tools dropdown items are MenuItems in OperatorWindow.xaml ToolsContextMenu, each with a Click handler in OperatorWindow.xaml.cs that opens a panel/dialog; ToolSearch_Click is the canonical 'host a UserControl in a new Window and ShowDialog' pattern to mirror. TemplateService.EnsureLoadedAsync already seeds the 3 built-ins and de-dupes against disk files by Id, so NO manual built-in seeding is needed. TemplateManagerPanel exposes a public ITemplateService? TemplateService setter that auto-refreshes.
